name: Do you need permits for a gut renovation in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Which parts of a gut renovation in Los Angeles usually require permits, and what happens if you skip them?
mainEntity.text: Which parts of a gut renovation in Los Angeles usually require permits, and what happens if you skip them?

acceptedAnswer.text: A gut renovation in Los Angeles usually needs permits whenever the project affects structure or building systems. That includes moving walls, altering load-bearing elements, replacing electrical service, changing plumbing routes, installing or relocating HVAC, and many window or opening changes. A simple cosmetic refresh may avoid permits, but a true gut renovation rarely does. The permit process also matters because inspections are tied to construction phases, and work cannot always proceed until prior items pass. Homeowners should verify permit responsibility in the contract, since the builder, designer, or homeowner may handle different parts of the process. The safest approach is to pull permits before demolition begins and keep approved plans on site during construction. This reduces delay, protects resale value, and limits problems when the home is sold later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Most gut renovations in Los Angeles require permits when they involve structural changes, plumbing, electrical, gas lines, HVAC, or major layout changes. Even interior-only work can trigger review if walls are removed or systems are upgraded. Skipping permits can cause stop-work orders, failed inspections, and expensive rework.
